What a big, fucking mess. What a big, fucking mess.

Might be the sudden clarity you get while incredibly tired in the middle of the night, but this realization, as obvious as it might seem, should carry the same weight as any other one: they are fabricating controversy for profit. They are the trolls that want attention. Why, why, why should they even be mentioned?

Before you reach the vote button of your choice, be aware that the paragraph above is stripped of any reference for two reasons: first, things like this have happened in the past, in different industries; second, if you recognized any possible affiliation, you might be in the mess too. If you are like me though, you want all of this to end. You want it all, the "factions", the injustice, the dangerous lies to dissolve naturally and not destroy everything around it in a big bang.

Do you know when you are just about to sleep, and maybe you live in a noisy area? The cars rolling on the asphalt, the lone steps on the sidewalk seem to fade away as you're drifting into sleep. Believe me, you can do that too with this ridiculous war, and keep the best bits, the ones that really deserve a discussion by experts, scientists, philosophers, and people interested.

Train yourself not to be outraged, as hard as it might seem. You might be someone who could relate to the topics discussed, and you might still chime in and offer your perspective, but still allow your mind to present your thoughts in the most mature, stoic and objective but personal way. Chances are people might listen to you and react in surprising ways. If you see a field you care about, let your best seed to be planted in it.

Keep yourself concentrated in what you like. This is your life after all, should you be forced to act in a certain way according to an internet mob? Only know that the law is your limit, the only limit that allows you to be a prosperous member of a society. Again, plant only the good seeds.

Make connections with as many people, as many minds, as many opinions as you possibly can, and digest what comes out of it. Listen, and carefully decide to dismiss what is not edible. The discussions might spawn an artichoke, know that it's got a delicious core.

Always try your best to get something good out of a mess. Even just acknowledging where the faults are is a good thing. Good engineers know which points in a bridge suffer the most pressure, let yourself be a good engineer for the bridge you, and hundreds, thousands of other people are going to create.

And don't forget to play. Games are works of art and open to interpretation. You are the one who makes the story.

Is there a way to show arrows to only people who are logged in/subbed/mods?

For un-logged in users, you can target something like .arrow-upvote[onclick="mustLogin();"].

But I would advise you not to do this. When an un-logged in visitor clicks on the arrows, they are prompted to register or login, which is good for the site's growth.

For unsubbed users, if you are concerned about brigading from other subs, that is a problem that should be solved on the server side (detecting unusual voting behaviour), and not by preventing users from expressing their votes on a public subverse.

For limiting voting only to mods... I don't see any reasonable use for that.
Thanks for the quick response. I just asked because it's how I used to write CSS back on Reddit. Having options open, you know? But I do see your point, so I won't do it. Thanks for the help! :)

No problem. If you want, for aesthetic reasons you could maybe fade out the arrows slightly for un-logged in users :) Thus still keeping their function of attracting new users.

The other thing to note is that whatever you do with custom CSS can be circumvented (either by disabling custom subverse styles in the account settings or manipulating the page in the browser), so it's really not an effective way to disable voting for any reason.
